title: Settle evaluation contracts before scanner flywheel
description:
As an evaluation owner, I want the corpus and fixture harness contracts settled in writing, so that later scanner work is steered by honest scores instead of alias tricks, unread files counted as misses, or two scorers that disagree.

This epic is for **design**, not for retuning detectors, adding PHP/Ruby ingest, or renaming Checkr. Those are scanner problems. We do not start using the evaluation system to improve the scanner until the questions on the child tasks have answers that code, gold YAML, and docs all implement.

## Why this exists

We imported 29 packets of gold into `DataParade-io/scanner` so a public `dataparade-cli` release could not wipe them. The corpus runner can produce per-layer numbers. Those numbers are still not a safe flywheel:

- Gold taxonomy keys (`pii:email_address`) and matcher rule ids (`mention:email`, `data_item:ssn`) are bridged by `tests/eval/identity.ts` aliases.
- Unread evidence can still enter recall if it appears on an exhaustive-scope list.
- `tests/eval/score.ts` and `tests/benchmark/precision.ts` do not implement the same match rules.
- Jest is five grades; corpus gold is four layers (`pii_signals` loaded as `mentions`, no `raw_hits` packets).
- Component and flow gold uses exact `type:name` keys, so vendor naming misses look like total recall failure.
- There is no frozen baseline of **evaluable (read) only** scores.

Child tasks are one issue each. Deep-thinking agents should argue the contract, propose a single decision, and list what must change in scorer, adapters, gold, and docs. They must not “fix” the scanner to make today’s messy scores look better.

## Out of scope

- Language ingest (PHP, Ruby, Swift, Rust) except as it affects the unread rule.
- Component naming quality (`third_party:checkr` vs `asset:requests call`) except as a documentedGap / naming-grade policy.
- Leftover proposed original-ten gold (incomplete corpus, not a harness contract).
- Making Plexus GraphQL eval run (a second client; align it after the scanner harness is the source of truth).

## Definition of done

Each child task has a recorded decision (and rejected alternatives). Follow-on implementation work is separate tasks. This epic closes when all six design questions are answered and the answers do not contradict each other.

Child design tasks (one question each, for multi-agent deep thinking — no scanner retune until decided):

1. KDATAP-d6eabf — One identity vocabulary for gold, adapters, and docs
2. KDATAP-791091 — Unread means ingest never opened the file
3. KDATAP-89d1a6 — One scorer for all headline metrics
4. KDATAP-f6b6e7 — One layer model for Jest and corpus
5. KDATAP-08a0ac — Policy for component and flow identity
6. KDATAP-955d82 — Frozen evaluable-only corpus baseline

comments.author: home
comments.text:
## Agreed evaluation-contract direction

Stakeholder discussion resolved the six design questions with one overarching rule: semantic normalization, eligibility, matching, and reporting are separate contracts and none may silently repair another.

The agreed architecture is:

1. Both gold and scanner findings map into a versioned canonical evaluation representation. Identity, classification, instance/vendor, evidence, and display names are separate. Broad aliases, labels-as-identity, and display-name matching are removed.
2. Eligibility is per layer and per canonical evidence path, with reasoned coverage outcomes. Exhaustive scope cannot make evidence readable.
3. One canonical evaluator performs deterministic one-to-one matching and owns recall, classification/label metrics, precision, negatives, unread, and unscorable reporting.
4. The headline product is a four-layer scorecard: mentions, repository-level data items, components, and data flows. Raw hits are diagnostic. No heterogeneous overall scalar is published.
5. Components and flows use structured taxonomy and graph identities, with a strict result plus diagnostic attribution. Partial detection does not become strict success, and locationless findings do not silently disappear.
6. Baselines are immutable contract-versioned artifacts with complete scanner, corpus, taxonomy, adapter, dependency, and source-SHA fingerprints. Contract changes receive bridge runs; detector changes never overwrite the reference baseline.

Two previously implicit requirements are now explicit:

- the unit and cardinality of an observation must be defined for every layer, because the current data-item collapse plus identity-only any-match scoring lets one finding satisfy multiple accepted gold cases;
- closed-world scope belongs to packet-and-layer review metadata, not only to positive annotations, so zero-positive reviewed scopes can measure false positives.

Rejected system-level alternatives are matcher vocabulary as truth, current gold strings as an unversioned contract, fuzzy equivalence groups, shared global read coverage, multiple scorers, five duplicated headline layers, opaque graph string aliases, and mutable incomparable baselines.

These comments settle design. Follow-on implementation work must be filed separately and should cover the canonical schema and migration, adapter/taxonomy maps, per-layer eligibility ledger, scope migration, one-to-one evaluator, four-layer runner, structured graph model, client de-duplication, and reproducible baseline artifacts. Scanner retuning and new language ingest remain outside this epic and must not begin from current scores.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
_Review pass recorded before the contract decisions were posted; kept for provenance. Where it conflicts with a decision, the decision governs — the follow-up comment below reconciles the two._

## Review pass over the six design questions (read-only; no code or gold changed)

Read the epic, all six children, `tests/eval/{identity,score,types}.ts`, `tests/benchmark/{precision,to-eval-cases,scan-repo,manifest,run-benchmark}.ts`, `src/ingest/file-system.ts`, `patterns/component-taxonomy.yaml`, and all 1,792 gold annotations across the 29 packets. Findings that change the shape of the queue, not just the answers.

### 1. Two of the four corpus layers are unscoreable by construction, not by policy

The epic frames components/flows as *"gold uses exact `type:name` keys, so vendor naming misses look like total recall failure."* Gold does not use `type:name`. It uses `type:<taxonomy subtype>`.

| gold component key shape | instances | share |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `type:<taxonomy subtype id>` (`asset:database` x182, `asset:api` x118, `asset:auth_service` x110, `asset:service` x41, `asset:cache` x14, `asset:config` x8, `actor:customer`, `actor:admin`) | 481 | 85% |
| `third_party:<vendor>` (auth0, stripe, supabase, sendgrid, paypal, checkr, ...) | 52 | 9% |
| `actor:user` — a role the taxonomy does not declare | 30 | 5% |

`componentIdentity()` emits `${type}:${name.toLowerCase()}`. So the exact-match rule tests the **vendor** question against gold that is 85% asking the **subtype** question. vgs-django's 0% is a category error, not a naming miss; no closed alias map repairs it, because the two sides are not naming the same kind of thing.

Data flows are worse: 424 distinct keys over 436 annotations, and **all 436 have bare endpoints** (`flow:user->stripe`, `flow:password->wp_check_password`, `flow:api-key->key_hash`, `flow:session->cookie`). The engine emits `flow:${type:name}->${type:name}`. Different grammar, and many gold endpoints are not components in any graph sense — a password is not a node. Every flow gold label is the generic `data_flow`, which `LAYER_GENERIC_LABELS` auto-passes, so flow label accuracy is a free 100% on anything that matches.

Detail and the recommended split are on KDATAP-08a0ac.

### 2. Root cause: the component taxonomy is half-adopted

```
Aug 28  6fab4d5  engine ported from dataparade-cli (componentIdentity = type:name)
Aug 30  4ca34cd  Add canonical component taxonomy
Aug 30           1,643 of 1,792 gold annotations authored, incl. 560 of 563 component
Aug 31  fc31a77  corpus gold + harness imported into scanner
```

Nothing in `src/` reads `patterns/component-taxonomy.yaml`. The only consumer anywhere is `tests/unit/taxonomy.spec.ts`, and it asserts one direction at test time: subtypes appearing in the classifier YAMLs are declared in the taxonomy. There is no runtime import, no validation of emitted components, and nothing that makes the taxonomy an output vocabulary.

The annotation agents (`composer-2.5-swarm`, `grok-4.6-fill-to-200`) adopted it the day it landed. The engine, ported two days earlier, never did. That is the whole component story: annotators speak taxonomy, the engine speaks instance names, and the scorer compares them with `===`.

### 3. The alias table carries most of PII recall, over a hard ceiling

15 PII rules total. Against them:

| layer | cases | exact rule id | alias-only | no rule exists |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| mentions (`pii_signals`) | 357 | 30 (8%) | **213 (60%)** | 114 (32%) |
| data items | 436 | 81 (19%) | 47 (11%) | **308 (71%)** |

Ceiling with today's rule set: ~68% mention recall, **~29% data-item recall**, perfect matching included. Detail on KDATAP-d6eabf.

### 4. Unread is larger than task 2 assumes and has two distinct causes

`FileLanguage` has no php, ruby or swift, and `ingestSingleFile` drops unknown types outright. 960 of 1,792 annotations (54%) sit on `.php` / `.rb` / `.xml` / `.swift`. Seven packets are essentially entirely unreadable: wordpress, magento, drupal, discourse, spree, redmine, vapor. Plus two wrinkles the ticket does not name — `scannedFiles` is a union of two different ingests, and the ingest caps produce absent files for a different reason than missing parsers. Detail on KDATAP-791091.

### Recommended change to the queue

The epic sequences 1 -> 6 with task 5 as a policy footnote. **Task 5 is the largest of the six** — it covers 999 of 1,792 annotations (563 components + 436 flows) and it is a regold decision, not a naming policy. Recommend promoting it and splitting:

- **5a components** — the answer is likely already written in KDATAP-0c4ab5: finish adopting the taxonomy on the engine side; eval identity becomes `${type}:${subType}`; vendor naming graded separately over the 52 `third_party:` cases.
- **5b flows** — likely: declare unscoreable, freeze out of headline numbers until regolded against component identity. Choosing "exact vs aliased" for a layer with 424 unique prose keys answers the wrong question.

Task 6 stays last, but its report shape needs a **reachability** column (see KDATAP-955d82) or the first published baseline will be read as detector quality when it is mostly vocabulary coverage.

### Correction to the epic body

The bullet *"Component and flow gold uses exact `type:name` keys"* is inaccurate and is steering task 5 at the wrong problem. Suggest: *"Component gold uses taxonomy subtype keys (`asset:database`) while the engine emits instance names (`asset:psycopg2`); flow gold uses bare prose endpoints the engine has no grammar for."*

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
## Measurements against the agreed contract

Re-read the six decisions after a full pass over `tests/eval/`, `tests/benchmark/`, `src/ingest/`, `patterns/component-taxonomy.yaml` and all 1,792 gold annotations. The architecture holds up against the data — the separation of normalization, eligibility, matching and reporting is the right cut, and one-to-one assignment resolves a real defect (identity-only any-match on data items).

What the decisions do not carry is size. Three of them are described as migrations "mechanical where unambiguous, adjudicated where ambiguous", and the corpus says the ambiguous share is the majority.

### Migration sizing

| gold | annotations | migration reality |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| components, `type:<taxonomy subtype>` | 481 | mechanical — rests are literal `component-taxonomy.yaml` ids |
| components, `third_party:<vendor>` | 52 | mechanical, and the only place gold asserts an instance |
| components, `actor:user` | 30 | **blocked** — `user` is not a declared subtype |
| data flows | 436 | **full regold** — 424 distinct bare-endpoint prose keys, no scorer identity at all |
| mentions | 357 | key migration mechanical; 339 need a decision on `subject.name` |
| data items | 436 | **308 are source names** (`id`, `uid`, `uuid`, `status`, `key`), not concepts — each needs adjudication |

The two bolded rows are roughly 750 annotations of human adjudication. That is the critical path of this program, and it is invisible in the decisions as written.

### One bucket the framework is missing

Eligibility reasons are ingest-shaped: successfully evaluated, unsupported, excluded, missing, read/parse error. There is no outcome for **gold whose concept the detector has no rule for**.

There are 15 rules in `patterns/pii-signals.rules.yaml`. Against them, **422 of 793** mention and data-item cases match no rule under any alias — `access_token` x39, `credential_secret` x29, `password_verifier` x13, plus the 308 data-item source names. The file was read successfully, so they are eligible; the detector has no concept for them, so they are permanent misses. Ceilings with today's rules: **~68% mention recall, ~29% data-item recall**, perfect matching included.

Agreed that raw recall must always include the miss (KDATAP-08a0ac is right to reject gap exclusion). The ask is narrower: report a **reachable** denominator alongside `evaluablePositives` as a diagnostic, never as an exclusion. Otherwise the first published number reads as detector quality when it is mostly taxonomy coverage, and the next session writes regexes for `uid` and `status`.

### `subject.name` needs a per-layer answer, not a global one

KDATAP-d6eabf rules that display names are never identity inputs and that `subject.name` may not rescue a key mismatch. Agreed for matching. But `subject.name` is not the same field on every layer:

- **mentions** — 339 of 357 carry a name that differs from the key, and it is the **source token the annotator saw**: `pii:access_token` / `id_token`, `pii:user_identifier` / `sub`, `pii:email_address` / `clientID`. That is precisely the source-name-vs-inferred-concept separation KDATAP-d6eabf calls for on data items. It should be **promoted into the canonical source-name field**, not discarded as a display name.
- **components** — all 563 carry a name; for the 473 assets it is a code instance (`directus_users`, `LocalAuthDriver`, `UsersService`, `appSession`).
- **data flows** — all 436 carry a name and it is genuine prose restatement of the key ("OIDC callback to session"). Discard.

A blanket "drop display names" destroys 339 mention annotations' worth of the only record of what was actually observed. Detail on KDATAP-d6eabf and KDATAP-08a0ac.

### Follow-on filing

The decisions list nine implementation workstreams. Recommend the sizes above ride on the corresponding issues when they are filed, and that the two adjudication blocks (436 flow regold, 308 data-item concept assignment) are filed as their own tracked work rather than folded into "migration", since they gate the first baseline and are human-bound rather than code-bound.

Also still open from the review, unaffected by the decisions: `project/wiki/four-layer-evaluation.md` is titled "Five-grade scanner evaluation", and `tests/eval/ground-truth-schema.md` line 27 asserts `conceptId === ruleId`, which the corpus contradicts. One doc pass closes both.
